buildBlocker: The installers are produced by .github/workflows/release-windows.yml, which needs the repository secret TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY. The repository currently has no secrets (actions/secrets total_count is 0), so that workflow cannot build signed artifacts yet.

The key cannot be generated fresh: the public half is pinned in src-tauri/tauri.conf.json and updater.requireSignedVersion is true, so a new key would sign packages no installed client accepts. It has to be the key that signed 0.1.17 (minisign key id 218D1940E2C4F3DC, verified against the published v0.1.17 signature).
Publishing a Release without latest.json would 404 the endpoint every installed client reads (releases/latest/download/latest.json) and break update checks, so no Release and no tag were created.
toFinishOnWindows: Add the repository secret TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY (plus TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD if the key has one). It must be the key that signed 0.1.17; do not generate a new one.

Dispatch .github/workflows/release-windows.yml. It runs the frontend and Rust suites, builds and signs 0.1.18 at the version already committed here, runs `npm run prepare:github`, and creates the Release with all five assets.
If publishing fails, the signed assets stay on the run as the artifact PulseWin-0.1.18-windows, so nothing has to be rebuilt.
Do not run `npm run release`: it bumps the patch version again and would skip 0.1.18.

Two test-side defects were fixed on the way: the status mock did not answer the new `status_pages` command, and `prompt cache countdown` raced its own fake clock (`install({time: T})` then `pauseAt(T)` throws "Cannot fast-forward to the past" once a millisecond has passed; it failed on pristine specs too, about one full-suite run in three).

windows.note: First Windows run of the suite, on the GitHub Actions windows-latest runner (.github/workflows/windows-check.yml, run 39440841593 at 8e7f6f5). The 35 tests that fail on macOS because they exercise Windows paths and PATH pass here, so this is a stricter bar than the macOS baseline. It found two real defects macOS could not compile or observe (a missing PathBuf import in the Windows-only system_path, and a path-as-identity comparison that gave one transcript two names by separator) plus three tests that assumed a POSIX host; all are fixed in their own commits. It does not build installers: the build step is --no-bundle.
